_readme: Settings for provisioning/dataverse/verify-solution-components.ps1 -Env dev ONLY —
deliberately NOT named dev-settings.json, for the same reason dev-schema-settings.json,
dev-auditing-settings.json and dev-scoring-settings.json are not: Get-ProvisioningSettings
-Env dev MUST keep throwing 'file not found'. ProvisioningCommon.Tests.ps1 asserts that
throw by name, and several scripts (verify-role-bindings.ps1, ensure-bulk-delete-jobs.ps1,
seed-settings.ps1) rely on it as the signal that DEV has nothing of that kind scripted
against it in Phase 1. verify-solution-components.ps1 reads THIS file directly on -Env
dev, bypassing Get-ProvisioningSettings entirely, so that invariant is undisturbed.
WHY A NEW DEDICATED FILE RATHER THAN REUSING dev-scoring-settings.json OR
dev-auditing-settings.json (both of which already carry tenantId/auth/environmentUrl for
DEV): this script's OWN scope is unrelated to scoring thresholds or audit retention, and
it needs no verification-specific key beyond the auth triplet and the environment URL —
the component list it checks live comes from source
(scripts/verify-solution-root-components.py --emit-json), never from a settings file.
Coupling it to a sibling script's settings file would mean an edit to that script's
own unrelated settings shape could silently break this one. Matches this repository's
own established pattern: one dedicated file per script, added 2026-08-14 onward
(IMP-0178 / improvement review 8, item 3).
wbs:6.8. IMP-0013 remediation — see the script's own header for the full story.
Identifiers only — never a secret, token or connection string (C-TECH-001). The
provisioning app id and certificate thumbprint stay in the environment variables named
under 'auth'.

dataverse._comment_environmentUrl: REV-GrantApplications-DEV, the same environment every other dedicated dev-*-settings.json file targets (e.g. dev-scoring-settings.json).
